errors.claim: The Community of Inquiry model is the framework that first identified the increasing learner role and importance of facilitating social and cognitive interactions.
searches: one of the first|first to identify|Community of Inquiry
increasing role of the learner|social and cognitive interactions
errors.source_check: The source calls Community of Inquiry "one of the first" frameworks to identify these points, not uniquely the first.
errors.suggested_fix: add qualifier "one of the first frameworks"

errors.claim: "Vegas rules" appears in the privacy-and-confidentiality framing of Chapters 4, 5, and 6.
searches: Vegas rules|what happens in the course
errors.source_check: "Vegas rules" appears in Chapters 4 and 5. Chapter 6 discusses trust, privacy, and confidentiality but does not use that phrase.
errors.suggested_fix: remove Chapter 6 from the "Vegas rules" attribution

errors.claim: The Guide frames privacy and trust as foundations, not as legal compliance.
errors.source_check: The source frames trust as foundational while also explicitly directing facilitators to consider institutional or organisational privacy and confidentiality policies; it does not contrast trust with compliance.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "The Guide frames trust as foundational alongside institutional privacy and confidentiality requirements."

errors.claim: Each course chapter (4-7) opens with a Facilitator Task List structured around "Several weeks (or months) before," "One to two weeks before," and "A few days before," followed by weekly operation.
searches: Several weeks \(or months\) before|One-? to two weeks before
A few days before|Before the course begins
errors.source_check: Only the Fundamentals material carries all three named timing stages. Design, Synchronous, and MicroCourses use different and less uniform pre-course structures, and the chapters do not open with their task lists.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "The course chapters organise facilitator work into pre-course, during-course, and post-course phases, with timing detail varying by course."

errors.claim: The Guide's directive is to prepare so the course can run lightly, rather than requiring the facilitator to run hard during delivery.
searches: available to the course on a daily basis
15 to 25 hours per week|preparation and implementation
errors.source_check: absent; the source instead specifies substantial during-course work, including daily availability and, for Fundamentals, 15-25 facilitator hours per week during preparation and implementation.

errors.claim: The five FLO courses are Fundamentals, Design, Synchronous, and MicroCourses, with compressed descriptions marked [V].
searches: Listed below are the five courses|The courses
errors.source_check: The source itself says "five courses" but enumerates only four named course types. The reference repeats that inconsistency, and its compressed descriptions are paraphrases rather than verbatim wording.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "The four named course types are ..." [AP], while noting that the source itself says five but lists four

errors.claim: FLO Fundamentals is the foundation; FLO Design and FLO Synchronous follow; MicroCourses run alongside.
searches: series of one-week MicroCourses|The collection includes
errors.source_check: The Introduction identifies two foundation courses (FLO Fundamentals and FLO Design), one in-depth course (FLO Synchronous), plus a series of one-week MicroCourses.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "FLO Fundamentals and FLO Design are the two foundation courses; FLO Synchronous is the in-depth course; MicroCourses form a one-week series."

errors.claim: Participation is full-time throughout, and participants are co-located with colleagues from various locations, settings, and disciplines.
searches: 6 - 12 hours per week|5 hours for course activities
errors.source_check: The source says participants "participate fully" throughout the course and "learn together" with colleagues from varied locations. It does not say participation is full-time or that participants are co-located; stated participant workloads are generally 5-12 hours per week.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "Participants participate fully throughout and learn together with colleagues from varied locations, settings, and disciplines."

errors.claim: Rachel Loganberg progressed from an observer role in the FLO Design pilot to co-facilitator and lead.
searches: ready to take the lead|went on to co-facilitate
errors.source_check: The source says Loganberg moved from observer to co-facilitator so that she would be ready to lead a future workshop; it does not say she had already become a lead facilitator.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "progressed from observer to co-facilitator, preparing to lead a future FLO workshop"

errors.claim: Facilitators ask teams "how do you think things are going, and maybe if they think something else needs to be done."
searches: how they think things are going|how do you think things are going
open-ended questions|something else needs to be done
errors.source_check: The source says "how they think things are going," not "how do you think things are going."
errors.suggested_fix: correct to the source wording "how they think things are going, and maybe if they think something else needs to be done"

errors.claim: The Weekly Participation Self-Assessment has a 15-per-week maximum and a 60-over-five-weeks maximum.
errors.source_check: The source is internally inconsistent: its prose says the maximum weekly total is 12, the weekly table cells say "out of 15," and the cumulative maximum is 60.
errors.suggested_fix: add qualifier that the source inconsistently reports 12 as the weekly maximum while its table rows say 15; retain the cumulative 60

errors.claim: FLO Design has implicit, cohort-sized class-size guidance.
errors.source_check: absent from the FLO Design chapter; "cohort" appears only in general advice to adapt expectations to cohort needs, not as class-size guidance.

errors.claim: FLO Synchronous accommodates 10 or more participants into the 20s with two facilitators.
searches: works well with 10 or more|into the 20s
most likely with two facilitators|class size
errors.source_check: The source says numbers into the 20s can be accommodated "most likely with two facilitators"; the reference drops that qualifier.
errors.suggested_fix: add qualifier "most likely with two facilitators"

errors.claim: About 6-8 of 20 FLO Synchronous participants should choose the Practicing Facilitator track.
searches: Ideally 6-8 participants or more|class size of 20
enough people choose the Practicing Facilitator track
errors.source_check: The source says "Ideally 6-8 participants or more," making 6-8 a floor-like target rather than the complete target range.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "ideally 6-8 participants or more out of a class of 20"

errors.claim: Across all four course chapters, the Guide returns to facilitator modelling as the load-bearing mechanism.
errors.source_check: Chapter 3 makes a general modelling claim, and explicit facilitator-modelling examples occur prominently in Fundamentals and Synchronous. The Design and MicroCourses chapters do not support the specific "all four course chapters" assertion.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "Across the Guide, especially Chapters 4 and 6, facilitator modelling is a recurring mechanism."

errors.claim: FLO Design facilitators plan their final synchronous session in the open by posting the lesson plan in a shared Google Doc.
searches: lesson planning for your final synchronous session
Google Doc or other shared site
errors.source_check: This passage appears in Chapter 6 and explicitly concerns the final session in FLO Synchronous, not FLO Design.
errors.suggested_fix: correct "FLO Design facilitators" to "FLO Synchronous facilitators"

errors.claim: Participants maintain Learning Journals throughout each course and share weekly nuggets in the Weekly Journal Share forum.
errors.source_check: Fundamentals uses Learning Journals and the Weekly Journal Share forum. Design uses personal journals optionally with a Weekly Reflections forum. Synchronous uses structures including 3-2-1, and MicroCourses does not prescribe the claimed journal/forum pattern.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "Fundamentals uses Learning Journals and Weekly Journal Share; Design may use journals with Weekly Reflections; the other courses use different reflection structures."

errors.claim: The Community of Inquiry connection is attributed to Garrison, Anderson, and Archer.
errors.source_check: Archer is absent from the source. The source names Anderson and Garrison in its bibliography and related discussion but never names or attributes the model to Archer.

errors.claim: Gomez-Rey, Barbera, and Fernandez-Navarro's identification of online-instructor roles corresponds to the FLO facilitator skill categories.
errors.source_check: The source explicitly says the role-based models "do not directly coincide" with FLO categories; only the individual skills show many similarities.
errors.suggested_fix: add qualifier that the role models do not directly coincide, although many individual skills overlap
